explanation.correct: A parsing error before any resource is created indicates a syntax/format problem in the template (malformed JSON/YAML, wrong indentation, or an invalid property); validate and lint the template.

distractors.B: Monitor resolution has nothing to do with template validation failures.
distractors.C: Physical power issues would not produce a template parsing error at a specific line.
distractors.D: A RAID battery is a storage-hardware concern, unrelated to template parsing.

explanation.exam_pattern: Parse/validation error before resources created = fix template syntax (JSON/YAML).

references: CompTIA Cloud+ CV0-004 Objectives: Domain 6 — Deployment issues (templates)

questions.stem: New instances launch successfully but all come up with an outdated application version and missing patches. The most likely culprit is:

options.text: A stale golden image that needs to be rebuilt/re-baked
The DNS TTL being too high

explanation.correct: If every new instance is outdated identically, the base/golden image is stale; re-bake it with current patches and the latest application build so new instances start current.

distractors.A: A load-balancing algorithm affects traffic distribution, not the software version baked into instances.
distractors.C: An expired certificate causes TLS errors, not an outdated application build on every new instance.
distractors.D: A high DNS TTL delays record changes; it does not install outdated software on new instances.

explanation.exam_pattern: Every new instance identically outdated = stale image; re-bake the golden image.

references: CompTIA Cloud+ CV0-004 Objectives: Domain 6 — Deployment issues (images)

questions.stem: A deployment to a new region fails to create resources. Which TWO are plausible deployment-stage causes to investigate? (Choose two.)

options.text: Insufficient quota/limits for the new region's resources
The company logo image is too large
A requested instance type or service is not available in that region
The end user chose a dark-mode theme in the console

explanation.correct: Region-specific failures commonly stem from a service/instance type not offered in that region, or from fresh regional quotas/limits that must be raised before resources can be created.

distractors.B: A logo image's size is irrelevant to deploying infrastructure resources.
distractors.D: A console theme choice has no effect on resource creation.

explanation.exam_pattern: New-region deploy fails -> check regional service availability and regional quotas.

references: CompTIA Cloud+ CV0-004 Objectives: Domain 6 — Deployment issues (capacity/region/quota)

questions.stem: Users can reach a server by its IP address but not by its hostname. Which subsystem is the most likely cause?

explanation.correct: Reachable by IP but not by name points to DNS: a missing/incorrect record, the wrong resolver, or propagation delay is preventing hostname-to-IP resolution.

distractors.B: A RAID array is about disk redundancy; it does not resolve hostnames.
distractors.C: Disk IOPS is a storage-performance metric, unrelated to DNS resolution.
distractors.D: Load-balancer stickiness affects session persistence, not name resolution.

explanation.exam_pattern: Works by IP, fails by name = DNS problem.

references: CompTIA Cloud+ CV0-004 Objectives: Domain 6 — Connectivity (DNS)

questions.stem: Two healthy instances in different subnets cannot communicate; packets are silently dropped. In cloud networking, what is the most likely first suspect to check?

options.text: Security group / network ACL rules and the route table

explanation.correct: Silently blocked traffic between subnets is most often a security group/NACL denying the port/protocol or a missing/incorrect route in the route table; verify the allow rules and routes first.

distractors.A: An object-storage lifecycle policy manages data retention, not inter-subnet connectivity.
distractors.C: CPU governor settings affect performance, not whether packets are permitted between subnets.
distractors.D: TLS cipher suites affect encrypted session negotiation, not basic subnet reachability.

explanation.exam_pattern: No traffic between subnets -> check security groups/NACLs and route tables first.

references: CompTIA Cloud+ CV0-004 Objectives: Domain 6 — Connectivity (firewall/routing)

questions.stem: A VPN tunnel is up and small pings succeed, but large data transfers hang or fail intermittently across it. Which issue is the classic cause?

options.text: An MTU/fragmentation mismatch (often needing MSS clamping)

explanation.correct: Small packets passing while large transfers stall over a tunnel is the hallmark of an MTU/fragmentation problem: encapsulation overhead lowers the effective MTU, so oversized packets with 'don't fragment' set are dropped. Lowering MTU or clamping MSS resolves it.

distractors.A: A missing tag affects cost reporting, not connectivity.
distractors.C: A stale image affects software versions on instances, not packet-size behavior on a tunnel.
distractors.D: An expired access key causes authentication failures, not size-dependent packet loss.

explanation.exam_pattern: Small packets OK, large ones fail over a tunnel = MTU/fragmentation; fix MTU or clamp MSS.

references: CompTIA Cloud+ CV0-004 Objectives: Domain 6 — Connectivity (MTU/latency)

questions.stem: Fill in the term: The time delay for a packet to travel from source to destination, which users experience as lag and which increases with physical distance between regions, is called ____ (one word).

explanation.correct: Latency is the time delay for data to traverse the network path; it grows with distance/hops and, when high, degrades interactive and chatty workloads. Placing resources closer to users (or using a CDN) reduces it.
explanation.exam_pattern: Network delay experienced as lag, rising with distance = latency (reduce via proximity/CDN).

references: CompTIA Cloud+ CV0-004 Objectives: Domain 6 — Connectivity (latency)

questions.stem: A database server's storage shows sustained 100% disk utilization with a long I/O queue, while CPU and memory are moderate. Which resource is the bottleneck?

explanation.correct: Saturated disk utilization with a growing I/O queue indicates a storage I/O (IOPS/throughput) bottleneck; remedies include faster disk tiers, more provisioned IOPS, caching, or spreading I/O.

distractors.A: Memory is moderate, so paging/exhaustion is not the indicated bottleneck.
distractors.C: DNS is a name-resolution service, not a disk-throughput constraint.
distractors.D: CPU is reported as moderate, so processing is not the constraint here.

explanation.exam_pattern: Disk at 100% with I/O queue = storage IOPS/throughput bottleneck.

references: CompTIA Cloud+ CV0-004 Objectives: Domain 6 — Performance (IOPS/throughput)

questions.stem: An application server becomes sluggish and the OS begins heavily swapping to disk; available RAM is near zero while CPU is not maxed. Which resource is constrained?

explanation.correct: Near-zero free RAM with heavy swapping is a memory bottleneck; the system pages to disk, hurting performance. Fixes include adding memory (vertical scale), tuning the app, or scaling out.

distractors.A: DNS-resolution issues cause name lookups to fail, not memory swapping.
distractors.C: Low free disk space causes write failures, not the paging/swapping signature of memory pressure.
distractors.D: Network-bandwidth saturation would show as network-throughput limits, not swapping.

explanation.exam_pattern: Low free RAM + heavy swapping = memory bottleneck.

references: CompTIA Cloud+ CV0-004 Objectives: Domain 6 — Performance (memory)

questions.stem: During peak load, a compute-heavy service shows sustained 100% CPU utilization and rising request latency, while memory and disk are fine. Which remediation most directly addresses the bottleneck?

options.text: Scale the compute (out by adding instances, or up to a larger CPU)

explanation.correct: Sustained 100% CPU with latency growth is a compute bottleneck; adding instances (scale out) behind a load balancer or moving to a larger CPU size (scale up) relieves it.

distractors.A: Object-storage versioning protects data; it does not reduce CPU load.
distractors.C: DNS TTL affects record caching, not CPU saturation.
distractors.D: Rotating a certificate addresses TLS trust, not CPU exhaustion.

explanation.exam_pattern: Sustained 100% CPU + latency = compute bottleneck -> scale out/up.

references: CompTIA Cloud+ CV0-004 Objectives: Domain 6 — Performance (CPU)

questions.stem: A monitoring dashboard is key to diagnosing performance issues. Which TWO metrics most directly identify a storage-throughput bottleneck? (Choose two.)

options.text: Disk throughput (MB/s) and I/O queue depth

explanation.correct: IOPS and disk throughput (with I/O queue depth) directly reveal storage-performance limits; when they plateau at the volume's maximum while the queue grows, storage is the bottleneck.

distractors.A: A TLS cipher reflects an encryption negotiation, not disk performance.
distractors.D: A DNS response code reflects name-resolution success, not storage throughput.

explanation.exam_pattern: Diagnose storage limits with IOPS, throughput (MB/s), and queue depth.

references: CompTIA Cloud+ CV0-004 Objectives: Domain 6 — Performance (storage metrics)
